title: Thomas Townsend Brown's thrust from asymmetric capacitors

tellings.quote: mid-century inventor Thomas Townsend Brown, who discovered that when you apply a high voltage to certain asymmetric capacitors, they produce thrust.

plain: Jesse Michels says that the mid-century American inventor Thomas Townsend Brown found something odd: if you put a high voltage across certain lopsided capacitors, which are devices that store electric charge between two plates of different shapes or sizes, they push themselves along and make thrust. Michels tells this himself, without naming a source, in an episode about Bob Lazar. If true, it would mean electricity alone could move an object without a propeller or rocket.
